## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` on the changed files and committed the formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable `AGENTS.md` Hard Rules; the allocating Torch-wrapper scope is explained below.
- [x] Labels: `cat-feature`, `area:sparse_attention`, `orig-external`, `mod-cutedsl`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL, existing Python BSA forward/backward APIs.

## Summary

Exact repeated neighborhoods in a blk64 sparse graph can use 128-wide MMA without requiring both axes to pair. This adds explicit `block_sparse_attention_blk64_prepare(...)` and an optional `blk64_plan=` argument to the existing forward/backward entry points.

- **FWD:** pair Q64 rows with identical KV neighborhoods. Load two arbitrary KV64 blocks through TMA into the existing KV128 shared-memory tile; QK and PV remain 128×128×128. Gather Q and scatter O/LSE only when needed.
- **BWD:** independently pair KV64 columns with identical reverse-Q neighborhoods. Keep KV ownership and loop over Q. Load two arbitrary Q64/dO64 blocks through TMA; all five MMA tiles remain 128×128×128. Gather K/V and scatter dK/dV only when needed. Odd Q degrees use a zero-contribution sentinel.
- Missing plans, unpairable directions and unsupported runtime declarations retain native dispatch. Native blk64 FWD/BWD kernel files are unchanged relative to `develop`.

Includes API docs, numerical/capture/fallback tests and **one standalone benchmark**, `benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py`. No benchmark directories or result files are added to the repository. The charts below are PR attachments.

## Why

Split TMA loads preserve the efficient 128-wide compute pipeline while relaxing the requirement for exact pairing on both axes. FWD needs only Q pairing, and BWD needs only KV pairing. Explicit preparation lets callers reuse routing analysis without adding discovery or synchronization to ordinary blk64 execution.

## Related issues

Based on `develop` at `ea97aab7`, including the native blk64 backward zero-fill/tail fix in #1682.

## API and compatibility impact

`blk64_plan` is appended as an optional keyword. The preparation function is lazily exported through `cudnn`, `cudnn.BSA` and `cudnn.torch`. The default forward/backward bodies are unchanged apart from the opt-in branch.

The paired path supports SM100/SM103, CuTe DSL >= 4.7, contiguous aligned BSHD BF16 tensors, MHA, D128, and full 128-token sequence tiles. SM100 was tested; SM103 was not available. Pair equality uses valid-prefix index sets, allowing reordered lists and nonadjacent pairs. Duplicate/out-of-range valid indices are rejected; unused capacity is ignored. Unsupported layouts, tails, block sizes or launch declarations fall back to native dispatch.

Preparation is explicit, blocking CPU analysis/upload outside graph capture. Reuse the plan with the same immutable routing/count tensors and fresh Q/K/V/dO storage; rebuild when routing changes. Ordinary Torch mutations are detected through version counters. Raw CUDA, captured writes and inference-tensor mutations remain the caller's responsibility.

**Hard-rule scope:** these are allocating standalone Torch wrappers, not workspace-based `execute()` APIs or graph engines. Warmed execution does not read device metadata on the host, performs no blocking CPU/GPU synchronization, runs on the operand device's current stream and supports CUDA Graph replay. Scratch is per call, and replay resets accumulators and odd-row sentinels. Caller-provided gradient outputs are honored. No topK/length cutoff is imposed; short topK=2 cases can be slower because fixed overheads are not amortized.

## Performance

Measured at `9b624cf3` on one idle NVIDIA B20Z / SM100 GPU: B=1, Hq=Hkv=40, D=128, BF16, Nq=Nkv=N, fully paired synthetic routing, bucket width 1024 Q64 blocks. Each configuration uses **3 seeds × 15 randomized rounds × 3 calls per CUDA Graph**, after 8 warmup replays. Clocks are unlocked.

This measures the **complete captured GPU path**, including permutations, resets, pre/postprocessing and native CSR construction. The grouped path reuses prepared CSR. CPU plan build, allocations, compilation and host enqueue time are excluded. Throughput is useful sparse work (`4 × B × H × N × topK × 64 × D` for FWD; factor 10 for BWD), not dense-equivalent work. Bars show medians of seed medians, with seed min–max error bars. Bar labels show TFLOPS and latency; the labels above each pair show the median within-seed speedup and throughput improvement percentage.

![FWD: native versus grouped blk64 throughput, latency and speedup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb9b3943-df98-4552-adc6-357b97f2a7ba)

![BWD: native versus grouped blk64 throughput, latency and speedup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4624357a-a594-4cc3-9a55-4a69d545dc12)

All 12 seed/configuration cases passed checks before and after timing: **120 tensor comparisons** against native blk64. Maximum relative L2: O **0.298%**, gradients **0.112%**. Independent FP64 oracle checks are covered by the test suite.

Plan construction is a separate blocking cost, including metadata transfer and CPU analysis:

![Explicit plan preparation cost across sequence lengths and topK](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe08da60-47ea-4650-aa30-49dedf0464a1)

These plan costs must be amortized by reusing unchanged routing. A plan rebuilt per layer/iteration can cost more than the GPU time saved; the FWD/BWD charts report GPU execution speedup with reusable metadata.

Reproduce (optional results go outside the checkout):

```bash
python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py \
  --lengths 32768 131072 --topks 64 256 --seeds 4593 4594 4595 \
  --rounds 15 --repeats 3 --output /tmp/blk64-grouped.jsonl
```

The same script supports `--sparsities .95 .90 .50 0`, independent `--patterns both q kv neither`, and separate forward/backward selection.


## Testing

Environment: NVIDIA B20Z / SM100, Torch 2.14.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2, cuDNN 9.24, CuTe DSL 4.7.1. Verified imports resolve to the tested checkout.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' \
  test/python/block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_blk64_plan.py \
  test/python/block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_attention_forward.py \
  test/python/block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_attention_backward.py
```

**76 passed, 93 skipped.** New coverage includes independent FP64-autograd O/LSE/dQ/dK/dV, independent Q/KV eligibility, variable valid counts, nonadjacent per-batch/head pairs, odd reverse degrees, unused NaN KV columns, asymmetric lengths, multiple buckets, changed scale/fresh pointer bindings, caller outputs, side streams, no warmed host reads, changed-input/poisoned-output capture replay, invalid/stale routing rejection and native fallbacks.

The standalone benchmark also passed a short N=512, H=2, topK=2 FWD+BWD smoke across all four pattern generators. `pre-commit run --files ...` passed Black, Black/Jupyter and SPDX checks; `git diff --check` passed. A fresh `import cudnn` does not import Torch, CuTeDSL or paired helpers. Source checks confirm native blk64 kernels are byte-identical to the current base and the blk128 BWD MMA/compute loops are unchanged.

+"""Compare native blk64 and explicitly grouped blk64 FWD/BWD on SM100/SM103.
+
+Install this checkout, then run on an idle GPU:
+    python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py --lengths 32768 131072 --topks 64 256
+    python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py --lengths 16384 32768 65536 131072 --sparsities .95 .90 .50 0
+    python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py --lengths 512 --topks 2 --heads 2 --seeds 4593 --rounds 3 --repeats 1
+
+Each direction compares the ordinary public API with/without ``blk64_plan`` on
+identical inputs. CUDA Graph timing includes GPU permutations, native CSR
+construction, resets and pre/postprocessing, and excludes CPU preparation,
+allocation, compilation and host enqueue time. Plan preparation is timed
+separately. Numbers are useful sparse TFLOPS, not dense-equivalent TFLOPS:
+FWD FLOPs = 4 * B * H * N * topK * 64 * D; BWD uses factor 10.
+
+Synthetic patterns force Q pairs, KV pairs, both, or neither. Pair discovery
+reports actual eligibility: additional pairs can occur, especially at 0%
+sparsity. Exact pairs need not be adjacent. Each row is sorted and unique.
+Warmup and measurement use randomized variant order. Reported throughputs are
+medians of seed medians; speedups are medians of within-seed latency ratios.
+Optional JSONL output contains provenance, per-round samples and accuracy
+checks. No results are written unless --output is supplied.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import random
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import time
+
+import torch
+import cudnn
+from cudnn.block_sparse_attention import api
+
+
+def make_routes(heads, blocks, topk, pattern):
+    qf = 2 if pattern in ("q", "both") else 1
+    kf = 2 if pattern in ("kv", "both") else 1
+    assert topk % kf == 0
+    scores = torch.rand((1, heads, blocks // qf, blocks // kf), device="cuda")
+    ids = scores.topk(topk // kf, dim=-1).indices
+    if kf == 2:
+        ids = torch.cat((ids, blocks - 1 - ids), dim=-1)
+    if qf == 2:
+        ids = torch.cat((ids, ids.flip(-2)), dim=-2)
+    return ids.sort(-1).values.int()
+
+
+def difference(actual, expected, *, lse=False, grad=False):
+    total_error = total_ref = maximum = 0.0
+    x, y = actual.reshape(-1), expected.reshape(-1)
+    for start in range(0, x.numel(), 8 * 1024**2):
+        a, b = x[start : start + 8 * 1024**2].float(), y[start : start + 8 * 1024**2].float()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, atol=1e-4 if lse else 0.03, rtol=1e-4 if lse else 0.03)
+        delta = a - b
+        maximum = max(maximum, delta.abs().max().item())
+        total_error += delta.square().sum().item()
+        total_ref += b.square().sum().item()
+    relative = (total_error / max(total_ref, 1e-30)) ** 0.5
+    assert relative < (0.001 if lse else 0.012 if grad else 0.008), relative
+    return dict(max_abs=maximum, relative_l2=relative)
+
+
+def measure(callables, rounds, seed, repeats=3):
+    """Randomized repeated-call graphs, warmed together before collecting samples."""
+    graphs, captured_outputs, samples = {}, {}, {name: [] for name in callables}
+    capture_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    capture_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.stream(capture_stream):
+            capture_order = list(callables)
+            random.Random(seed).shuffle(capture_order)
+            for name in capture_order:
+                fn = callables[name]
+                fn()
+                fn()
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                captured_outputs[name] = []
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                    for _ in range(repeats):
+                        captured_outputs[name].append(fn())
+                graphs[name] = graph
+            # Sustained GPU work before measurement avoids a cold first variant.
+            for _ in range(8):
+                for graph in graphs.values():
+                    graph.replay()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            rng = random.Random(seed)
+            start, end = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2)]
+            for _ in range(rounds):
+                order = list(graphs)
+                rng.shuffle(order)
+                for name in order:
+                    start.record()
+                    graphs[name].replay()
+                    end.record()
+                    end.synchronize()
+                    samples[name].append(start.elapsed_time(end) / repeats)
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for graph in graphs.values():
+            graph.reset()
+    return {name: dict(median_ms=statistics.median(values), samples_ms=values) for name, values in samples.items()}
+
+
+def run_case(args, n, topk, pattern, seed):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    q, k, v, dout = [torch.randn((1, n, args.heads, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(4)]
+    routes = make_routes(args.heads, n // 64, topk, pattern)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    plan = api.block_sparse_attention_blk64_prepare(routes, num_kv_blocks=n // 64, bucket_size_blocks=args.bucket_size_blocks)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    plan_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
+    kwargs = dict(layout="bshd", sparse_block_size=64)
+    out, lse = api.block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, routes, **kwargs)
+    functions = {
+        "fwd": {
+            "native": lambda: api.block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, routes, **kwargs),
+            "grouped": lambda: api.block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, routes, **kwargs, blk64_plan=plan),
+        },
+        "bwd": {
+            "native": lambda: api.block_sparse_attention_backward(dout, q, k, v, out, lse, routes, **kwargs, bucket_size_blocks=args.bucket_size_blocks),
+            "grouped": lambda: api.block_sparse_attention_backward(
+                dout, q, k, v, out, lse, routes, **kwargs, bucket_size_blocks=args.bucket_size_blocks, blk64_plan=plan
+            ),
+        },
+    }
+    record = dict(
+        n=n,
+        topk=topk,
+        pattern=pattern,
+        seed=seed,
+        sparsity=1 - topk * 64 / n,
+        plan_ms=plan_ms,
+        eligible=dict(fwd=plan.forward_enabled, bwd=plan.backward_enabled),
+        reason=dict(fwd=plan.forward_reason, bwd=plan.backward_reason),
+    )
+    directions = ("fwd", "bwd") if args.direction == "both" else (args.direction,)
+    for direction in directions:
+        callables = functions[direction]
+        reference = callables["native"]()
+
+        def check():
+            return [
+                difference(a, b, lse=direction == "fwd" and i == 1, grad=direction == "bwd") for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(callables["grouped"](), reference))
+            ]
+
+        before = check()
+        timings = measure(callables, args.rounds, seed + (direction == "bwd"), repeats=args.repeats)
+        for timing in timings.values():
+            timing["tflops"] = (4 if direction == "fwd" else 10) * args.heads * n * topk * 64 * 128 / timing["median_ms"] / 1e9
+        speedup = timings["native"]["median_ms"] / timings["grouped"]["median_ms"]
+        record[direction] = dict(timings=timings, speedup=speedup, accuracy_before=before, accuracy_after=check())
+        print(
+            f"N={n} topK={topk} pattern={pattern} seed={seed} {direction.upper()} "
+            f"native={timings['native']['tflops']:.1f} grouped={timings['grouped']['tflops']:.1f} TFLOPS "
+            f"speedup={speedup:.3f}x eligible={record['eligible'][direction]} plan={plan_ms:.1f} ms",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+    return record
+
+
+def summarize(records):
+    print("\n| N | topK | sparsity | pattern | direction | native ms | grouped ms | native TFLOPS | grouped TFLOPS | speedup | plan ms |")
+    print("| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |")
+    cases = dict.fromkeys((r["n"], r["topk"], r["pattern"]) for r in records)
+    for n, topk, pattern in cases:
+        rows = [r for r in records if (r["n"], r["topk"], r["pattern"]) == (n, topk, pattern)]
+        for direction in ("fwd", "bwd"):
+            if direction not in rows[0]:
+                continue
+            values = [
+                statistics.median(r[direction]["timings"][variant][metric] for r in rows)
+                for metric in ("median_ms", "tflops")
+                for variant in ("native", "grouped")
+            ]
+            speedup = statistics.median(r[direction]["speedup"] for r in rows)
+            plan_ms = statistics.median(r["plan_ms"] for r in rows)
+            print(
+                f"| {n} | {topk} | {rows[0]['sparsity']:.2%} | {pattern} | {direction.upper()} | "
+                + " | ".join(f"{v:.3f}" for v in values)
+                + f" | {speedup:.3f}x | {plan_ms:.1f} |"
+            )
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument("--lengths", nargs="+", type=int, default=[32768, 131072])
+    density = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
+    density.add_argument("--topks", nargs="+", type=int, default=None)
+    density.add_argument("--sparsities", nargs="+", type=float, help="Fractions removed; round to the nearest positive even topK")
+    parser.add_argument("--patterns", nargs="+", choices=["both", "q", "kv", "neither"], default=["both"])
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=40)
+    parser.add_argument("--seeds", nargs="+", type=int, default=[4593, 4594, 4595])
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=15)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3, help="Calls per CUDA Graph; use 1 for long dense cases to limit storage/work")
+    parser.add_argument("--bucket-size-blocks", type=int, default=1024, help="Backward bucket width in Q64 blocks, matching the native API")
+    parser.add_argument("--direction", choices=["both", "fwd", "bwd"], default="both")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="Optional JSONL path outside the source tree")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if any(n <= 0 or n % 128 for n in args.lengths) or min(args.heads, args.rounds, args.repeats, args.bucket_size_blocks) <= 0:
+        parser.error("lengths must be positive multiples of 128; heads, rounds, repeats and bucket size must be positive")
+    if args.sparsities is not None and any(not 0 <= s < 1 for s in args.sparsities):
+        parser.error("sparsities must be in [0, 1)")
+    if args.sparsities is None:
+        args.topks = [64, 256] if args.topks is None else args.topks
+        if any(k <= 0 or k % 2 or k > min(args.lengths) // 64 for k in args.topks):
+            parser.error("topks must be positive even counts <= the shortest sequence's KV64 block count")
+    cases = []
+    for n in args.lengths:
+        topks = args.topks if args.sparsities is None else [max(2, min(n // 64, 2 * round((1 - s) * (n // 64) / 2))) for s in args.sparsities]
+        if len(set(topks)) != len(topks):
+            parser.error(f"duplicate topK cases after rounding at N={n}")
+        cases.extend((n, k, pattern) for k in topks for pattern in args.patterns)
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        parser.error("requires an available SM100 or SM103 GPU")
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+    expected_api = root / "python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/api.py"
+    if Path(api.__file__).resolve() != expected_api.resolve():
+        parser.error(f"cudnn imports from {api.__file__}; install this checkout before benchmarking")
+    sources = [Path(__file__), expected_api, *sorted((root / "python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention").glob("_blk64*.py"))]
+    sources += [
+        root / f"python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/csrc/{direction}/sm100_blk{block}/bsa_{direction}_sm100.py"
+        for direction in ("fwd", "bwd")
+        for block in (64, 128)
+    ]
+    try:
+        commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=root, text=True).strip()
+    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
+        commit = None
+    provenance = dict(
+        gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        gpu_uuid=str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).uuid),
+        torch=torch.__version__,
+        cutedsl=importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl"),
+        cudnn_path=cudnn.__file__,
+        commit=commit,
+        sha256={str(p.relative_to(root)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sources},
+        settings={k: str(v) if isinstance(v, Path) else v for k, v in vars(args).items()},
+    )
+    print(json.dumps(dict(provenance=provenance)), flush=True)
+    output = args.output.open("x") if args.output else None
+    records = []
+    try:
+        if output:
+            output.write(json.dumps(dict(provenance=provenance)) + "\n")
+            output.flush()
+        for n, topk, pattern in cases:
+            for seed in args.seeds:
+                record = run_case(args, n, topk, pattern, seed)
+                records.append(record)
+                if output:
+                    output.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+                    output.flush()
+                gc.collect()
+                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    finally:
+        if output:
+            output.close()
+    summarize(records)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

 BSA is implemented with Python CuTe DSL/JIT kernels.
 
+The ordinary blk64 entry points accept an explicit
+[`blk64_plan`](#prepared-pairs-in-the-blk64-path). It enables split 64-row TMA
+loads with unchanged 128-wide MMA tiles, independently for forward and backward.
+
+## Prepared pairs in the blk64 path
+
+```python
+from cudnn.torch import (
+    block_sparse_attention_blk64_prepare,
+    block_sparse_attention_forward,
+    block_sparse_attention_backward,
+)
+
+# Explicit CPU analysis, outside capture/timing; rebuild when routing changes.
+# q/k/v/dout are contiguous BSHD BF16 tensors with D=128.
+plan = block_sparse_attention_blk64_prepare(
+    q2k_block_index,
+    num_kv_blocks=k.shape[1] // 64,
+    q2k_block_nums=q2k_block_nums,  # optional valid-prefix counts
+    bucket_size_blocks=1024,      # Q64 blocks, i.e. 65,536 Q tokens
+)
+kwargs = dict(
+    q2k_block_nums=q2k_block_nums,
+    sparse_block_size=64,
+    layout="bshd",
+    blk64_plan=plan,
+)
+o, lse = block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, q2k_block_index, **kwargs)
+dq, dk, dv = block_sparse_attention_backward(dout, q, k, v, o, lse, q2k_block_index, **kwargs)
+```
+
+| Direction | Exact pairing needed | Global GPU permutations | Compute geometry |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| FWD | Each Q64 neighborhood has even multiplicity and a positive even valid length | Q gather, O/LSE scatter; K/V retain original order | QK/PV both 128×128×128; K/V load as 64-row pieces |
+| BWD | Each KV64 reverse neighborhood has even multiplicity; Q rows are nonempty | K/V gather, dK/dV scatter; Q/dO/O/LSE retain original order | All five MMA tiles 128×128×128; KV stationary, loop Q; Q/dO load as 64-row pieces |
+
+Pair equality compares **sets of valid indices**, so list ordering need not
+match. Preparation validates prefixes and rejects duplicate or out-of-range
+valid indices. Padding after the valid prefix is ignored. Pairing is all-or-none
+for each direction across all batch/head entries. `plan.forward_enabled`,
+`plan.backward_enabled` and their corresponding `*_reason` fields describe
+graph eligibility. A Q-only plan can accelerate only FWD; a KV-only plan can
+accelerate only BWD. The other direction calls the original implementation.
+Odd backward degrees use a zero-contribution second Q64 half, and unused KV
+columns produce zero dK/dV. Identity permutations skip gather/scatter kernels.
+
+The paired implementation supports SM100/SM103, CuTe DSL >=4.7, BF16 MHA D128,
+contiguous aligned BSHD inputs, and sequence lengths divisible by 128. Other
+layouts, tails, `block_sizes`, FWD `kv_splits != 1` or an explicit `use_clc`, and
+backward outputs with unsupported strides retain native dispatch. An explicit
+backward `bucket_size_blocks` different from the plan's bucket width also uses
+native dispatch. There is no topK/length performance cutoff: paired topK=2
+inputs also use the new path. On short sequences BWD can be slower because
+packing and initialization are not amortized. `blk64_plan` requires
+`sparse_block_size=64`.
+
+No plan is built implicitly. With `blk64_plan=None` (the default), the original
+kernels, launch parameters, metadata construction and allocation path remain
+unchanged; the paired module is not imported. This avoids charging arbitrary
+blk64 calls for discovery, synchronization or permutations.
+
+**Lifetime and costs:** preparation copies routing metadata to the CPU and
+builds GPU permutations/CSR. The plan owns routing metadata, not Q/K/V storage,
+and can be reused with fresh Q/K/V/dO pointers. Pass the same routing tensors,
+count tensor and fixed-count argument used at preparation. Rebuild the plan
+whenever the sparse graph changes. Ordinary Torch in-place changes are rejected
+using host version counters; changes through raw CUDA pointers, captured graph
+writes or inference tensors cannot be detected and violate this immutable
+metadata contract. Do not modify the plan's private tensors.
+
+These are allocating Torch wrappers, not workspace-based `execute` APIs.
+They allocate outputs and scratch per call; optional `dq_tensor`, `dk_tensor`
+and `dv_tensor` still receive the gradients. No mutable execution scratch is
+shared between calls/streams. Warm the exact configuration before CUDA Graph
+capture. Replay resets accumulators and odd-row sentinels every time. GPU
+permutations and reset/pre/postprocessing are part of execution; CPU preparation
+and first-call compilation must be measured separately. Rebuilding a CPU plan
+per layer/iteration can outweigh the GPU saving; use this explicit path when
+the mask can be reused, and benchmark the complete workload.
+
+Use [`benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py`](../../benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_grouped.py)
+to compare native and planned FWD/BWD, including GPU permutations and
+pre/postprocessing. It reports explicit plan preparation separately.

+import torch
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda
+
+from cudnn._torch_stream import record_streams
+from cudnn.frost.compiled_cache import compile_cached
+from ._blk64_reorder import reorder
+from ._interface import _to_cute_tensor_with_dynamic_modes

+from .csrc.bwd.sm100_blk128.bsa_bwd_sm100 import BlockSparseAttnBackwardSm100Blk128, BsaK2qCsrTensors

+@cute.kernel
+def _post_dq_kernel(accum, output, scale: cutlass.Float32):
+    block, head, batch = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    thread = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(32):
+        flat = thread + i * 256
+        row, column = flat // 128, flat % 128
+        # Two independent Q64 reductions from the unchanged M128 TMEM tile.
+        src = cutlass.Int64(block) * 8192 + (column // 32) * 2048 + (column % 32 // 4) * 256 + row * 4 + column % 4
+        output[batch, block * 64 + row, head, column] = (accum[batch, head, src] * scale).to(output.element_type)
+
+
+_post_dq_kernel.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _post_dq(accum, output, scale: cutlass.Float32, stream):
+    _post_dq_kernel(accum, output, scale).launch(grid=(output.shape[1] // 64, output.shape[2], output.shape[0]), block=256, stream=stream)
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _init_tail_kernel(lse, delta):
+    head, batch, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    row = lse.shape[2] - 64 + cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
+    lse[batch, head, row] = cutlass.Float32(float("inf"))
+    delta[batch, head, row] = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+
+
+_init_tail_kernel.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _init_tail(lse, delta, stream):
+    _init_tail_kernel(lse, delta).launch(grid=(lse.shape[1], lse.shape[0], 1), block=64, stream=stream)
+
+
+def _signature(args):
+    # Shapes/strides/dtypes and optional declarations only; no data or pointers.
+    return tuple(
+        (tuple(x.shape), tuple(x.stride()), str(x.dtype)) if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) else type(x).__name__ if x is not None else None for x in args
+    )
+
+

+        kernel,
+        *[to_cute_tensor(x) if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) else x for x in args],
+        cute.runtime.make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False),
+        cache_key=f"bsa_blk64_paired:{name}:{_signature(args)}",
+        options="--enable-tvm-ffi",

Thank you for your contribution! The exact coarsening preserves the attention graph, and the explicit preparation/permutation contract is clear. I found no approval-blocking issue. Forward and backward preserve original ordering, including independent batch/head permutations, and reuse prepared sparse metadata without host reads during warmed execution. Keeping this opt-in is appropriate: preparation cost and the short-list permutation overhead matter, as the documentation explains.

Validation: Native SM100, 68 SMs, Python 3.10, Torch 2.11.0+cu128, CuTe DSL 4.7.0 and cuDNN 9.27. Exact-head Python imports verified; reused a built extension only after proving its C++/header/build inputs identical. No compatibility aliases. The grouped and existing BSA forward/backward L0 selection plus kernel-name tests gave 52 passed, 33 skipped and 76 deselected. Includes independent FP64 O/LSE/gradient references, variable counts, unused NaN KV, side streams and changed-input CUDA Graph replay. Nine additional checks passed: exhaustive coarsening of all 50,625 nonempty-row 4x4 binary graphs (61 accepted, each matching an independent pairing predicate and exact edge reconstruction), plus eight native cases covering coarse degrees 1/2/3/4 and one/multiple backward buckets. Same-shape A→B→A metadata changes and captured A replay interleaved with B remained correct for O, LSE and every gradient after changing Q/K/V/dO and poisoning outputs. Three bounded native64-versus-grouped performance cases passed numerical checks at B=1, H=4, N=8192, D=128 BF16, topK=8/32/128. Whole-call GPU graph replay includes grouped permutations and backward resets. At topK=8 grouped forward/backward took about 86.8/247.8 us versus 72.1/237.1 us; at topK=128, 328.1/942.8 us versus 421.4/1823.5 us. The topK=32 forward difference overlaps repeated-control variation. Grouped eager host enqueue was measured separately (about 84–270 us forward and 132–452 us backward, including allocation). These unlocked-clock spot checks support the documented workload dependence, not a universal speedup. Checked the public exports, admission and version gates, element/Int64 address arithmetic, stream ordering, CSR ownership and accumulator reset paths. Verified the 27 submitted benchmark records' sample medians/FLOP formulas and all nine source hashes, including the two precisely documented post-measurement edits. The consumed BSA/cache/stream contracts are unchanged between merge-base and reviewed base.

Limitations: No native SM103 or multi-GPU validation, and no reproduction of the author's 131K/H40 B20Z or CAKE measurements. The 33 skipped cases are not validated by this run.
